blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Deflation refers to a sustained decrease in the general price level of goods and services.
Disinflation represents a reduction in the rate of inflation, meaning prices are still rising but at a slower pace.
Stagflation occurs when high inflation combines with stagnant economic growth and high unemployment.
Both monetary measures by the RBI and fiscal measures by the Government are required to address these macroeconomic imbalances.

blocks.content: Deflation refers to a sustained, continuous and general fall in the price level of goods and services in an economy over a period of time. It is not a temporary fall in prices but a long-term decline.
Deflation is the exact opposite of inflation. While inflation reduces the purchasing power of money, deflation increases the purchasing power of money.

• General fall in prices

• Continuous process

• Increase in purchasing power of money

• Reduction in economic activity

1. Fall in Money Supply:

When RBI or banks reduce money supply, demand falls and prices decline.



2. Fall in Aggregate Demand:

Low income, unemployment and pessimism reduce demand.



3. Credit Contraction:

Banks reduce lending, which reduces spending.



4. Reduction in Government Expenditure:

Lower public spending reduces overall demand.



5. Excess Production:

When supply exceeds demand, prices fall.

• Producers suffer due to falling profits

• Investment declines due to low returns

• Unemployment increases

• Economic growth slows down

• Debt burden increases in real terms
Disinflation refers to a reduction in the rate of inflation. Prices continue to rise, but at a slower pace than before.
Disinflation does NOT mean fall in prices. It simply means that the speed of price rise has reduced.

• Prices are still rising

• Inflation rate is falling

• Purchasing power still declines but slowly

• Considered healthy for economy

• Tight monetary policy by RBI

• Increase in interest rates

• Controlled money supply

• Improved production and supply

• Controls excessive inflation

• Improves economic stability

• Encourages long-term investment

• Maintains growth with stability

rows: Often accompanied by low demand and recessionary pressures
Rising price level, but at a slower pace
Controlled economic growth under policy moderation
Stagnant economic growth accompanied by high unemployment

blocks.content: Stagflation refers to a situation where inflation and economic stagnation occur simultaneously. It is characterised by rising prices, low economic growth and high unemployment.
Stagflation is dangerous because policies used to control inflation may worsen unemployment, and policies used to increase growth may increase inflation.

• Supply shocks such as oil crisis

• Increase in production costs

• Structural weaknesses in economy

• Inefficient economic policies

• High inflation with unemployment

• Decline in output

• Policy dilemma for government and RBI

• Loss of public confidence in economy

Inflation: Prices rise continuously

Deflation: Prices fall continuously

Disinflation: Prices rise at decreasing rate

items: Distinguish carefully between Deflation (negative inflation) and Disinflation (slowing inflation rate) in conceptual MCQs.
Stagflation presents a policy dilemma because traditional counter-inflationary measures can worsen unemployment and economic stagnation.
Focus on monetary policy actions taken by the RBI and fiscal intervention tools used by the Government to manage price stability.

blocks.content:
Inflation: Growth may continue

Stagflation: Inflation + stagnation + unemployment
PART E: ROLE OF RBI AND GOVERNMENT

• RBI uses monetary policy tools to manage inflation and disinflation

• Government uses fiscal policy to address deflation and stagnation

• Stagflation requires careful balance of both policies

• Deflation = fall in general price level

• Purchasing power rises in deflation

• Disinflation = fall in inflation rate

• Prices still rise in disinflation

• Stagflation = inflation + stagnation + unemployment

• Stagflation is most dangerous economic condition
